title: Composition of the canonical derived scalar mates
statement: Let Λ, Γ, Δ be commutative condensed ring objects and b:Λ→Γ, c:Γ→Δ monoid homomorphisms [def-sfb-derived-push-hom]. Suppose that at every scheme the two scalar-extension functors preserve finite limits. Write a_b,T and a_c,T for the canonical derived extension/levelwise restriction adjunctions [def-sfb-derived-extend-levelwise-adjunction]. For any g:U→V and M in D(Mod(Λ_U)), the inverse mate under the composite adjunctions a_b,U.comp a_c,U and a_b,V.comp a_c,V of the horizontally pasted inverse restriction/direct-image squares [def-sfb-derived-comap-lower-star-iso] equals Lc_V.map((derivedPushHom b g).app M) followed by (derivedPushHom c g).app(Lb_U.obj M). No geometric scalar mate is assumed invertible. The canonical adjunction constructors and the component identity are the declarations recorded here. The restriction squares retain the published moduleObjectDerivedPushforward notation [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]; these are exactly the usual total right derived lowerStar functors.

proof.text: Construct each adjunction by derivedExtendMapDerivedCategoryAdjunction; the ambient module tensor and resolution structures are those in NativeProperScalarMateData. Its canonical right adjoint is levelwise restriction. Compose the two adjunctions. Retain the published moduleObjectDerivedPushforward names in the restriction square before forming mates; these are exactly the usual right derived lowerStar functors, and do not change the construction.

By the definitions of derivedPushHom and pushHomOfComapIso, each individual inverse mate of the inverse derivedComapLowerStarIso is exactly the specified derivedPushHom. The flatness assumptions supply these comparisons.

Apply Mathlib mateEquiv_hcomp to the two individual inverse mates, apply the inverse equivalence to the resulting equality, and evaluate at M. Expand the component of vertical pasting using associator, whiskering and identity component formulas. Substitute the two individual identifications to obtain the displayed successive scalar-extension formula. This is proved entirely in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem nativeScalarDerivedCompositeMate
    {Λ Γ Δ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1}}
    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ] [MonObj Γ] [IsCommMonObj Γ]
    [MonObj Δ] [IsCommMonObj Δ]
    (b : Λ ⟶ Γ) (c : Γ ⟶ Δ) [IsMonHom b] [IsMonHom c]
    [∀ T : Scheme.{u}, PreservesFiniteLimits (Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap b T))]
    [∀ T : Scheme.{u}, PreservesFiniteLimits (Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap c T))]
    {U V : Scheme.{u}} (g : U ⟶ V)
    (M : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (ProEt.topology U) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj Λ U))) :
    ((mateEquiv (nativeScalarDerivedCompositeAdjunction b c U)
        (nativeScalarDerivedCompositeAdjunction b c V)).symm
      ((nativeScalarDerivedRestrictionSquare c g).hComp
        (nativeScalarDerivedRestrictionSquare b g))).natTrans.app M =
      (Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap c V)).leftDerivedFunctor.map
          ((CondensedRing.derivedPushHom b g).app M) ≫
        (CondensedRing.derivedPushHom c g).app
          ((Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap b U)).leftDerivedFunctor.obj M)
